chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: A Harlem day and night: recording, Mrs. Frazier's, after-hours spots
summary: He describes his daily round of recording, eating, clubs, Uptown House, Wells and waiting for the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then I had an opportunity...this is my day, this would be my schedule. I'd have a recording date at 9 o'clock. From 9 to 12. I'd go back home, eat breakfast, go back to bed. Wake up at 6. Come out to Mrs. Frazier's restaurant where a lot of people used to eat 'cause there were not that many places to eat. You couldn't eat in Frank's in those days, or you could, but you knew you'd have to be with some white person, all right? Go to Mrs. Frazier's and eat, after I go to Mrs. Frazier's and eat, 6 o'clock, may go down on Broadway to a show or go to a play, or they may have a party for Trevie Woods or somebody coming into town, all right? And after that if you were working you'd go to work, say, at 10 o'clock, and if you were not working you'd go hang around with some of the Cotton Club girls, or the Zanzibar or the Ubangi or Small's Paradise, or something, all right? And then when you'd leave there you would...say it's after the closing time...we'd go to Mary Lou William's and John* had a- rib-joint on Seventh Avenue--
*Mary Lou's husband at the time, John Williams, saxophonist with the Andy Kirk orchestra.
we'd go to Jimmy's Chicken Shack up on the hill, or you'd go, you know, places like that.

All right, now. They'd have like...each club would have like a breakfast...not a breakfast dance but a breakfast show they would call it. Or you'd go to Clarke Monroe's Uptown House, or you'd go to...let me see.. Clarke Monroe's Uptown House...I'm trying to think of that boy that was in love with Tallulah Bankhead...what was his name...There were two places that you could go. And if you'd happen to do that you'd see--you'd go to Clarke's Uptown House* you'd see Mickey Rooney, or Cary Grant, Art Tatum, Billie Holiday, Jimmy Monroe, Canada Lee, you know, celebrities like that. Duke Ellington, Billy Strayhorn, Sonny Greer. Each one surrounded by idol-worshipers, you know what I mean. Each one with an entourage. Now, you said, "Okay, where can we go now." You leave there, you go to Wells for chicken and waffles, all right? And so forth and so on. Then you'd go to bed.

On Friday you didn't go to bed. You went straight through from that routine that I told you, from the beginning, but at 8 o'clock you would go to somebody's apartment and drink, or someplace, and wait for the Apollo Theatre to open for the first show, you know, because that first show, Dan, you'd get more. They'd always...they'd have maybe like a couple of acts. After every first show, usually, some act was cut off. A couple of acts. Because it'd be too long...you got to cut this down.....

+Sugar Hill, a modestly well-to-do section in the western part of Harlem.
*i.e.- Clark Monroe's Uptown House.
